title: Cairo Stopover: What to See in 24 or 48 Hours
excerpt: A Cairo layover tour works: the Pyramids, Sphinx and Grand Egyptian Museum in one 8-hour day from €71 (Nov 2026), plus old Cairo with 48 hours. Two timelines and airport logistics.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

Yes, a Cairo layover tour is realistic. With 24 hours you can see the Giza Pyramids, the Sphinx and the Grand Egyptian Museum on one guided day of about 8 hours. With 48 hours, add Coptic Cairo, the Citadel and the Khan el-Khalili bazaar. Land the evening before, sleep in Giza, and fly out the night your tour ends. If you leave the airport you need an Egyptian visa, so arrange it before you fly.

Check current UK government travel advice for Egypt before making your arrangements; advice can change.

Key facts

Fact Detail
Where Cairo and Giza: the Pyramids, the Sphinx and the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) all sit on the Giza side of the city
Time needed 24 hours: one full touring day (Pyramids and GEM) · 48 hours: adds Coptic Cairo, the Citadel and Khan el-Khalili
Main tour Giza Pyramids, Sphinx & the Grand Egyptian Museum: about 8 hours, hotel pickup included
Typical cost From €71 per person with an Egyptologist guide, transport, both entry tickets and lunch, as listed in November 2026
Airport Cairo International (CAI) is in Heliopolis, about 22 km from the city centre and roughly 40 km from Giza. Uber and Careem both operate there
Visa Leaving the airport means entering Egypt: a visa is needed unless your nationality is exempt. Check the current fee on the official e-visa portal
Best time October to April, cool and clear; summer tours start early to beat the heat

Join it on Sawa Giza Pyramids, Sphinx & the Grand Egyptian Museum, from €71 per person, as listed in November 2026

You have a day, maybe two, between flights at Cairo International. Is it enough to see anything real? Yes, if you plan around two facts: the Giza Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum sit together on the Giza side of the city, and a guided day absorbs the traffic that ruins do-it-yourself timing. Below are two realistic timelines, 24 and 48 hours, built around the Giza and GEM tour, plus the airport logistics that decide whether the plan holds. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform, lists these tours; its founder has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

Cairo stopover in 24 or 48 hours: the quick answer

Choose by hours on the ground. A 24-hour stopover gives one full touring day, and the right day is the Pyramids plus the GEM: the museum stands about 2 km from the pyramids plateau, so both fit one loop. A 48-hour stopover adds old Cairo (Coptic churches, the Citadel, Khan el-Khalili) at a pace that still catches your flight. With fewer than about ten hours between flights, we would skip the tour idea, because immigration and traffic take too much of the time.

24 hours in Cairo: the Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum in one day

The 24-hour plan works when your single free day is a tour day: land the evening before, sleep in Giza, tour for about 8 hours, and fly out that night. On the Giza and GEM tour the day runs in this order:

  1. Evening before: land and sleep in Giza. Clear immigration, take an Uber or Careem (ride-hailing apps) to a Giza-side hotel. The airport is about 40 km from the pyramids, and the drive takes roughly 45 minutes in light traffic and up to two hours at peak times.
  2. Hotel pickup. Your Egyptologist guide and the vehicle collect you; entry tickets for the Pyramids and the GEM and lunch are included. The pyramid interior and camel rides are not.
  3. The Giza plateau. The pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, the panorama point where the three align, then the Great Sphinx and Valley Temple.
  4. Lunch, included, on the way to the museum.
  5. The Grand Egyptian Museum. A guided visit to a museum described as the world's largest devoted to a single civilisation, and the first place to display Tutankhamun's complete collection together.

Who the 24-hour plan suits

Travellers with one night and one free day between flights, and anyone on a late-evening flight out. The honest limit: no old Cairo. With one day, the pyramids win.

48 hours in Cairo: adding old Cairo at a human pace

Day 1 stays as the 24-hour plan above; Day 2 moves into old Cairo: Coptic churches in the morning, the Citadel after lunch, Khan el-Khalili late afternoon, with an unhurried start. A realistic Day 2, on your own by Uber or Careem between stops:

  1. Morning: Coptic Cairo. The Hanging Church and Egypt's oldest Christian quarter, set within the walls of a Roman fortress.
  2. Midday: the Citadel of Saladin. Saladin's hilltop fortress and the Muhammad Ali Mosque, with the city below; the mosque of Sultan Hassan stands nearby.
  3. Late afternoon: Khan el-Khalili. A bazaar dating from the fourteenth century and still trading; go in late afternoon as the heat drops.
  4. Evening: dinner on the Nile, on the roughly 2-hour Nile Dinner Cruise with a buffet, from €48 per person (drinks extra), or the Fancy Nile Dinner Cruise from €79, both as listed in November 2026; or head straight to the airport for a night flight.

A gentler split: two half-days

If one eight-hour day sounds too much, split it: the roughly 4-hour Giza Uncovered tour (from €29, plateau ticket included) covers the plateau on Day 1; the roughly 3-hour Secrets of the Grand Egyptian Museum tour (from €48, general admission included) fills Day 2 morning. Prices are per person, as listed in November 2026. GEM tickets are sold online only, so the guided tours handle that for you; if you go independently, our Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum in One Day guide has the plan and the ticket rules.

Cairo airport logistics: visas, Uber and luggage

Cairo International Airport (CAI) has three terminals, immigration can be slow at busy times, and road times swing with traffic, so treat everything below as planning minimums.

  • Visa first. Leaving the airport means entering Egypt. Most nationalities need a visa, either on arrival or as an e-visa from Egypt's official e-visa portal. Fees have changed recently and a further rise has been reported for January 2027, so check the current fee there rather than on third-party sites. Passport validity rules apply too, so check them with your airline. Staying airside on a connecting ticket generally needs no visa; confirm with your airline.
  • Terminals. Terminal 3 is the newest and the main base for EgyptAir and its Star Alliance partners; Terminals 1 and 2 handle most other international carriers. Check your boarding pass, as assignments change. Some airlines fly into Sphinx International Airport on the western side of Cairo instead, so check which airport your flight uses.
  • Uber and Careem. Both apps run from the airport to central Cairo and Giza, with a signposted pickup zone outside arrivals at each terminal. You pay in-app, which ends fare haggling. Expect roughly EGP 150 to 300 (about €2.50 to €5 at EGP 60 to the euro, 8 November 2026) to central Cairo in about 25 to 45 minutes, and more, and slower, to Giza and at rush hour.
  • Luggage. Ask your Giza hotel to hold bags for you for the day, even before check-in. Left-luggage services at the airport are not something we could confirm, so check with the airport or your airline. Take a small day bag.
  • Buffers. Our advice, not official guidance: allow about 3 hours at the airport before an international flight, and never book a tour that ends less than 5 hours before departure.

Three tips most stopover guides miss

  • Book the tour for your middle day, not landing day. A morning pickup on arrival day assumes immigration and traffic behave; tour the next day instead.
  • Sleep in Giza, not by the airport. If the pyramids are the mission, a Giza-side hotel means one short ride each way, not two city crossings.
  • The GEM pairing makes 24 hours viable. The Grand Egyptian Museum stands about 2 km from the pyramids plateau, so Pyramids plus GEM is one loop, not two drives across Cairo.

The verdict on your Cairo stopover

One full day in Cairo covers the Pyramids, the Sphinx and the Grand Egyptian Museum; two days add old Cairo without rushing. Land the night before, sleep in Giza, sort your visa before you fly, and let a shared departure absorb the traffic. faq.q: What can I do on a Cairo stopover?
faq.a: In 24 hours: the Giza Pyramids, Sphinx and Grand Egyptian Museum on one guided day of about 8 hours. In 48 hours: add Coptic Cairo's Hanging Church, the Citadel of Saladin and Khan el-Khalili bazaar. A guided tour absorbs the traffic; Uber or Careem cover the airport runs.

faq.q: Do I need a visa if I leave Cairo airport during a layover?
faq.a: Almost always yes. Exiting the airport means entering Egypt, so most nationalities need a tourist visa: either a visa on arrival or an e-visa arranged in advance on the official portal , which also shows the current fee. Staying airside on a connecting ticket is generally the visa-free case. Confirm your nationality's rules and the current fee before booking any stopover tour.

faq.q: Is 24 hours enough for the Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum?
faq.a: Yes. They pair naturally because the GEM stands about 2 km from the Giza plateau. One guided day of about 8 hours covers both: the pyramids and Sphinx, lunch, then the museum, from €71 with both tickets and lunch included. The constraint is your flights: arrive the night before, depart late.

faq.q: Is Uber available at Cairo International Airport?
faq.a: Yes. Uber and its regional equivalent Careem operate from Cairo International to central Cairo and Giza, with pickup zones outside arrivals. You pay in-app, which avoids fare haggling. Build in slack: the airport-to-Giza run takes roughly 45 minutes in light traffic and can double at peak.

faq.q: Where can I leave my luggage during a Cairo stopover?
faq.a: The easiest place is your Giza hotel, which will normally hold bags for the day if you are a guest, even before check-in. Airport left-luggage services are less certain, so check with the airport or your airline. Pack a small day bag and leave the main suitcase where you sleep.

faq.q: What happens if my Sawa departure does not fill?
faq.a: Nothing is charged before the date confirms, and reserving a seat is free. A date has until seven days before the tour to reach four travellers. If it does not, it is cancelled, you pay nothing, and Sawa suggests another date. Once confirmed, it is not cancelled for low numbers.
